publisher: California Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control
ownership: Official state alcoholic-beverage licensing records published as a daily machine-readable export
catalog_license: California state-created website information is generally public domain unless otherwise indicated
source_access: Public anonymous read-only HTTPS download refreshed each business day. The ABC page explicitly offers raw fixed-width and CSV downloads of pending and active license records.
allowed_use: official HTTPS metadata and archive download
normalization of source rows marked both ACTIVE and LIC
derived source-linked registry assertions and relationships
redistribution of aggregate statistics with publisher attribution and semantic limitations
prohibited_use: representing ABC ACTIVE as independent proof of continuous operation, public access, current hours, solvency, or compliance
representing alcohol licenses as every business in California or the United States
representing application rows as issued licenses
counting multiple active license-type rows for one File Number as multiple premises
silently overriding source ACTIVE when an expiration date predates observation
publishing record-level natural-person names or possible residential premises without approved privacy review
retaining or publishing mailing addresses from the raw archive
inferring ownership, parent company, network affiliation, or cross-source identity without versioned evidence
attribution: Source: California Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control, Daily Data Export, Licensing Reports.
retention: Retain immutable privacy-minimized selected-source and governed normalized releases. Delete the raw downloaded archive after selected-field staging.
redistribution: Aggregate counts may be redistributed with California ABC attribution, exact refresh/checksum, and license-scope limitations. Record-level normalized data remains local-review-only because licensee names can identify people and premises can be residences.
personal_data_handling: Primary licensee names may be natural persons and premise addresses may be residences. Mailing fields are discarded before staging; normalized record-level artifacts remain local-review-only.
